sectionProgressions.description: Stepwise Andalusian-style minor descent (bVII - bVI - v) resolving back into the tonic A minor instead of a major dominant

A natural minor sustained-note melody emulating the EBow solo phrasing

harmonicFunction: Am7 (i7) - Minor tonic softened by the open G and E strings for a dreamy, floating center
Fmaj7 (bVImaj7) - Lush submediant major-7th chord sharing the A, C, and E triad of Am
G6 (bVII6) - Subtonic chord with open B and E strings creating a suspended, weightless lift
Em7 (v7) - Minor dominant chord preserving the cool, understated Aeolian mood without a harsh G# leading tone

techniques.name: 12-String Style Open-Drone Strumming & Arpeggiated Extensions
techniques.description: Weaving picked bass notes with shimmering upper-string strums so the open B and high E strings act as a continuous harmonic halo across every chord change

sequence: Strike the root bass note on beat 1 of each chord before brushing across the treble strings
Keep the high E string (and often the B string) open as you shift from Am7 to Fmaj7 to G6
In the chorus, walk the bass smoothly down from G (3rd fret) to F (1st fret) to open E before landing on Am7
Add delicate 16th-note upstrokes to emulate the rich double-course chime of a 12-string acoustic
tips: Arch your fretting fingers steeply on Fmaj7 (X-3-3-2-1-0) so the open high E string rings clearly
Use a thin-to-medium pick (0.60mm) to get a feathery, percussive 12-string brush on a 6-string guitar
Engage a subtle chorus pedal or 12-string simulator if playing on a standard 6-string

techniques.name: Marty Willson-Piper & Peter Koppes Melodic EBow / Synth-Guitar Phrasing
techniques.description: Infinite-sustain melodic phrasing using an EBow or volume swells, navigating the A natural minor (Aeolian) scale with weeping slides and bagpipe-like Celtic inflections

notes: Target evocative 9th (B) and 4th (D) degrees on strings 2 and 3
Slide smoothly along the G string: 5 -> 7 -> 9, and B string: 8 -> 10 -> 12 -> 13
Continuous infinite sustain mimicking the Synclavier-processed bagpipe effect
sequence: Position the EBow directly over the G string for continuous string vibration
Slide between notes without picking to preserve the unbroken, vocal-like glide
Apply gentle, slow fret-hand vibrato to bloom each sustained note into the reverb wash
tips: Use an analog delay set to around 380ms with 4 repeats to float behind the lead line
If playing without an EBow, use a compressor/sustainer pedal and pick very softly near the neck
Emphasize the mournful Celtic mood by taking your time on the transitions

sections.name: Intro 12-String Shimmer & Ambient Drone
sections.description: Karin Jansson and Steve Kilbey's iconic opening progression floating through Am7, Fmaj7, G6, and Em7 with ringing open treble strings.
notes: Let the open high E and B strings ring continuously across all four chords
Keep your strumming hand flowing in a relaxed 126 BPM 16th-note wave
Emphasize the dreamy major-7th color of Fmaj7

sections.name: Verse 1 Nocturnal Strumming
sections.description: Steve Kilbey delivers the immortal opening lines ('Sometimes when this place gets kind of empty...') over shimmering acoustic drones.
notes: Play with gentle, hypnotic dynamics
Ensure the open high E string sounds clearly across the Fmaj7 mini-barre
Lock smoothly with the low bass pulses on beats 1 and 3

sections.name: Chorus 'Wish I Knew'
sections.description: The chorus descends stepwise down the A natural minor scale ('Wish I knew what you were looking for...') through G, Fmaj7, and Em7 to Am7.
notes: Highlight the descending bass notes: G (3rd fret) → F (1st fret) → E (open) → A (open)
Notice how resolving Em7 to Am7 creates a wistful, unresolved pull
Repeat the four-chord cycle twice per chorus

sections.name: Verse 2 Interlocking Electric Arpeggios
sections.description: Marty Willson-Piper and Peter Koppes layer delicate Rickenbacker clean arpeggios that interlock seamlessly with the acoustic rhythm bed.
notes: Pick cleanly through the inner strings with alternate picking
Let each note ring and overlap like a celestial harp
Use subtle chorus and analog delay for stereo width

sections.name: Iconic EBow / Synth-Guitar Solo
sections.technique: Marty Willson-Piper & Peter Koppes Melodic EBow / Synth-Guitar Phrasing
sections.description: One of the most haunting instrumental solos in rock history. Created using an EBow on an electric guitar processed through a Synclavier to simulate Celtic bagpipes, soaring through A natural minor with infinite sustain, slow weeping slides, and poignant Aeolian melodies.
notes: Slide up the G string (frets 5 -> 7 -> 9) with sustained, unbroken tone
Ascend the B string through the poignant 9th (12th fret B) and minor 3rd (13th fret C)
Let the note weep into the plate reverb before descending gracefully
Resolve softly onto the A minor tonic triad

sections.name: Final Chorus & Fading Starlight Outro
sections.description: The song glides toward infinity as Kilbey's vocals echo into the distance and Koppes weaves shimmering high-octave lead phrases above the cyclical strumming.
sections.progression: G - Fmaj7 - Em7 - Am7 (repeating to ambient fade)
notes: Maintain the hypnotic, steady 16th-note strumming flow
Add high 12th-fret single-note ornaments on the top strings
Let the final Am7 chord ring out into quiet silence

guitar.recommended: Takamine or Maton 12-String Acoustic + Rickenbacker 360/12 (Marty Willson-Piper & Peter Koppes)
guitar.pickup: Acoustic piezo blended with condenser mic, plus neck humbucker/EBow for lead

amp.recommended: Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus or Vox AC30

effects.distortion: Smooth sustain compression/overdrive for the solo
effects.other: EBow (Electronic Bow) for the solo section and lush stereo chorus

beginner.title: Open-Position Extended Chords
steps: Practice keeping the high E string ringing clearly on every chord
Play the chorus walkdown (G - Fmaj7 - Em7 - Am7) at 100 BPM
Strum through the full song at 126 BPM

intermediate.title: Thumb-Wrapped Fmaj7 & 16th-Note Brush
steps: Add the low F bass note on the 6th string 1st fret for a full 6-string Fmaj7 (1-3-3-2-1-0)
Integrate picked bass notes on beat 1 with 16th-note treble strumming
Explore high-neck drone voicings like Amadd9 (X-0-7-5-0-0)

advanced.title: 12-String Texture & Legato Solo
steps: Weave Peter Koppes's electric arpeggio counter-lines around the acoustic rhythm
Perform the ambient solo using legato slides or an EBow
Control dynamics from the hushed opening verse to the cinematic bridge peak

commonMistakes: Accidentally muting the open high E string with the side of your index finger on Fmaj7
Playing a standard E major (E7) in the chorus instead of the cooler, modal Em7
Strumming too aggressively with a heavy pick and losing the delicate 12-string chime
practiceRoutine: 3 minutes: Am7 → Fmaj7 → G6 open-string clarity check (pluck each string individually)
5 minutes: Chorus G → Fmaj7 → Em7 → Am7 descending bass walkdown
4 minutes: Legato solo melody on strings 2 and 3
5 minutes: Full song playthrough at 126 BPM
focusAreas: Uninterrupted open-string drone across chord changes
Modal Aeolian v7 to i7 chorus resolution
metronomeWork: Practice at 100 BPM focusing on fluid 16th-note wrist motion
Increase to 115 BPM while maintaining bass-note accuracy
Play at album tempo of 126 BPM with effortless dynamic flow
